reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch Re-Harden (mat_g1_na_q4_6), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: All generated items faithfully require solving single-step word problems involving the addition or subtraction of money amounts. For instance, addition is directly tested in seed 43 ("Kuya Ton had ₱2 and received ₱1 more from Nanay. How much money does Kuya Ton have in all?") and seed 44 ("Isko has ₱10 in one pocket and ₱6 in another pocket. How much money does Isko have in total?"). Subtraction is directly tested in seed 42 ("Marco had ₱5 in a piggy bank and used ₱1 to buy a notebook. How much money is left in the piggy bank?") and seed 501 ("Kuya Ton had ₱50 in a piggy bank and used ₱39 to buy a notebook. How much money is left in the piggy bank?"). Every sample adheres to 1-step arithmetic with money values within bounds.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set demonstrates comprehensive coverage across both required arithmetic operations (addition and subtraction of Philippine peso values) as well as diverse everyday contexts. Scenarios include combining amounts in pockets ("Bianca has ₱10 in one pocket and ₱10 in another pocket. How much money does Bianca have in total?" - seed 50), purchasing items and finding total cost ("Moses bought a pencil for ₱10 and an eraser for ₱1. How much did Moses spend in all?" - seed 601), and spending money with remaining change ("Nanding had ₱60 and bought a snack for ₱40 at the sari-sari store. How much money does Nanding have left?" - seed 500; "Ate Nena had ₱10 and spent ₱1 on bags of flour at the palengke. How much money does Ate Nena have left?" - seed 46).

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The cognitive demand and reading difficulty are exceptionally well-calibrated for Grade 1 Quarter 4 learners. Sentence structures are short, clear, and feature familiar Philippine cultural and household settings (e.g. Nanay, piggy bank, sari-sari store, palengke). The questions are straightforward single-step problems without extraneous or distracting information, such as in seed 603 ("Sir Ben bought a pencil for ₱2 and an eraser for ₱1. How much did Sir Ben spend in all?") and seed 604 ("Faye had ₱1 and received ₱6 more from Nanay. How much money does Faye have in all?").

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The samples show robust variant coverage, incorporating multiple semantic problem structures: joining/receiving amounts ("Faye had ₱1 and received ₱6 more from Nanay. How much money does Faye have in all?" - seed 604), aggregation of parts across different locations ("Des has ₱10 in one pocket and ₱10 in another pocket. How much money does Des have in total?" - seed 602), finding total expenditure ("Riza bought a pencil for ₱5 and an eraser for ₱1. How much did Riza spend in all?" - seed 605), and take-away/remaining subtraction from stored funds ("Carlo had ₱80 in a piggy bank and used ₱2 to buy a notebook. How much money is left in the piggy bank?" - seed 502). The evaluation format also spans multiple-choice (mcq) and fill-in-the-blank (cloze) formats.

competency_alignment.rationale: All sampled items strictly match the MATATAG learning competency statement without exceeding scope. Problems strictly involve single-step addition or subtraction of money, avoid complex multi-step reasoning, avoid non-money units or fractional centavos, and stay strictly within the bounds of sums up to ₱100 and subtraction amounts less than ₱100. For example, seed 45 ("Chef Demi saved ₱10 on Monday and ₱1 on Tuesday. How much money did Chef Demi save altogether?") and seed 600 ("Kuya Renz had ₱10 and bought a snack for ₱2 at the sari-sari store. How much money does Kuya Renz have left?") perfectly mirror the competency scope.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Numerical scales are fully aligned with the competency constraints (addition sums ≤ ₱100, subtraction minuends and subtrahends < ₱100). The samples range from small single-digit additions like ₱2 + ₱1 = ₱3 in seed 43 ("Kuya Ton had ₱2 and received ₱1 more from Nanay. How much money does Kuya Ton have in all?") to two-digit subtractions like ₱80 - ₱2 = ₱78 in seed 502 ("Carlo had ₱80 in a piggy bank and used ₱2 to buy a notebook. How much money is left in the piggy bank?") and ₱60 - ₱40 = ₱20 in seed 500 ("Nanding had ₱60 and bought a snack for ₱40 at the sari-sari store. How much money does Nanding have left?"), ensuring appropriate progression without breaching limits.
